set.body:
Objective

Freeze the evidence pairing as a normative architecture contract before production refactoring:

E_LR(H, K) = <H, B_L K B_R^T>_F = <B_L^T H B_R, K>_F.

Scope and deliverables

- Add a normative evidence-pairing contract defining the four identified spaces, forward transport, Frobenius adjoint, conceptual second-order lift, open and closed boundaries, reversal, partial materializations, and operation order.
- State precisely how the certified effect-form contract is recovered when the neural boundary is closed.
- Define structural capabilities separately from sample-dependent diagnostics.
- Define axis-aware normalization roles and forbid silent movement across nonlinear transforms or partition reduction.
- Add independent dense oracle helpers and deterministic contract, differential, metamorphic, randomized, and adversarial fixtures.
- Include negative fixtures for rank-one normalized-connectivity degeneracy, same-shaped but differently identified axes, forged positivity, and attempted default Kronecker materialization.

Acceptance evidence

- Adjoint contraction, vectorization, partial-application, reversal, direct-sum, bridge, and scalar-equivalence laws pass against code independent of production kernels.
- Randomized fixtures cover rectangular unequal-axis relations and factored H and K.
- The contract states that B_R tensor B_L is conceptual only.
- Existing effect-form laws remain unchanged and passing.
- No public API or connectivity engine is introduced in this stage.

Ownership boundary

Own the new normative contract and independent oracle/test fixtures. Production compiler, kernel, result, and public API changes belong to later epics.

Deferred non-goals

No production measurement_form, no optimized lowering, no connectivity terminology, no learned measurement, and no reconstruction API.
set.title: Epic 1: Freeze evidence-pairing semantics and executable laws
